title: SceneAgent: An Agentic Pipeline from 3D and 4D Captures to Simulation Environments
abstract: arXiv:2610.34745v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Visual captures provide detailed scene appearance, but converting them into interactive simulation environments requires object reconstruction, physical modeling, and correction of intermediate errors. We present SceneAgent, an agentic pipeline that coordinates these steps through simulator-based visual inspection and repair. The pipeline processes 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), photogrammetry, LiDAR captures, AI-generated 3DGS scenes, and 4D videos of dynamic scenes, and combines object segmentation, physical parameter estimation, part decomposition, articulation, and deformable simulation. To support policy learning, SceneAgent generates diverse object variants ("digital sisters") and scripted demonstrations. On a cluttered bin scene from GraspClutter6D, SceneAgent raises F1 at 1 cm for every coding agent with scorable outputs both with and without its skills, and its reconstructions are better than SimFoundry: all agent configuration

translated_title: SceneAgent：从3D与4D采集到仿真环境的智能体流水线
translated_abstract: 视觉采集能够提供精细的场景外观，但要将其转化为可交互的仿真环境，需要物体重建、物理建模以及对中间错误的修正。我们提出了SceneAgent，这是一个智能体流水线，通过基于仿真器的视觉检查与修复来协调这些步骤。该流水线可处理3D高斯泼溅（3DGS）、摄影测量、LiDAR采集、AI生成的3DGS场景以及动态场景的4D视频，并融合了物体分割、物理参数估计、部件分解、铰接建模与可变形仿真。为支持策略学习，SceneAgent能够生成多样化的物体变体（“数字姊妹”）以及脚本化演示数据。在一个来自GraspClutter6D的杂乱料箱场景上，对于所有具有可评分输出的编码智能体，无论其是否使用本流水线的技能，SceneAgent都提升了其在1厘米阈值下的F1分数，且其重建质量优于SimFoundry的所有智能体配置。
tldr: SceneAgent是一个智能体流水线，能够通过基于仿真器的视觉检查与修复，将3DGS、摄影测量、LiDAR、AI生成场景及4D视频等多种视觉采集自动转化为物理可交互的仿真环境，并通过生成物体变体与演示数据支持策略学习，其重建质量优于SimFoundry。
en_tdlr: SceneAgent is an agentic pipeline that converts diverse 3D/4D visual captures (3DGS, photogrammetry, LiDAR, AI-generated scenes, and 4D videos) into physically interactive simulation environments via simulator-based visual inspection and repair, generating object variants and scripted demonstrations to support policy learning, with reconstructions outperforming SimFoundry.
